scientific_question: Can denser calibrated rays plus a fixed classical spectral prior turn the valid but field-inadequate v156 proxy into a meaningful reconstruction reference before any warm predictor is trained?
role: post-open private controlled proxy development; not real experimental pairing

inputs.model_calibration_pairing: complete 9 x 13 cross-product; never infer a true match
inputs.field_preprocessing: subtract global mean, then divide by global RMS

operator.observation: two transverse gradient line integrals per valid ray
operator.adjoint: exact Euclidean transpose of stored COO weights

spectral_controls.transform: orthonormal three-dimensional DCT-II coefficients with inverse DCT-III lift
spectral_controls.primary: DCT1024-CGLS K16 at 24x24 rays per camera

metrics: p50/p90-higher/worst by arm, ray density and camera count

independent_recomputation.solvers: standalone BP, full CGLS, DCT CGLS and Jacobi PCGLS

decision_order: Any operator, observation, accounting or independent-recomputation failure makes v157 inconclusive.
A failed DCT1024 oracle closes this spectral representation before reconstruction claims.
A valid proxy but failed primary adequacy gate blocks warm-predictor training; matching a poor K4 reference is not useful progress.
Only a fully independently verified primary pass authorizes a separately frozen minimal CPU predictor.
No result may infer a true PT-to-calibration match or claim real BOST without paired two-dimensional measurements.
